text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA

- Stable prices and dinar exchange rate in April are proof that tasks set out in the country's economic policy were fully implemented earlier in the year, says Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic.
- Experts attending Yugoslav-Macedonian border demarcation talks are to draft an international agreement which will be concluded by the two governments.
- Yugoslav-Russian trade was doubled in 1996 to $800 million and is expected to exceed one billion dollars in 1997, said Russian trade representative in Belgrade.
- Yugoslav and Bulgarian airlines agree to open direct air links between Sofia and Belgrade.
- Yugoslav fruit and vegetable producers expect to export goods worth $164 million this year, which is five percent more than in 1996.

- Yugoslav government is called on to take measures to check uncontrolled steel imports which are jeopardising domestic steel producers, said Miodrag Pejovic, director of Montenegrin steel plant Zeljezara Niksic.
- Yugoslav government submits 1996 final budget statement to federal parliament under which it realised 93.7 percent of its 9.238 billion dinar budget, 371.4 million dinars less than planned.
- Newsprint and cellulose factory Matroz from Sremska Mitrovica received $5 million loan from Austrian partner.

- New-York based American Express bank and Belgrade Komercijalna banka AD concluded an agreement Monday under which the Belgrade bank will issue American Express travellers cheques and nostro cheques enabling Yugoslav firms to make non-cash payments abroad.

- Acting general manager of Beogradska banka, which groups 20 banks, Borka Vucic said she was preparing to reorganise her bank to make it more functional, to unify foreign payment operations, but this did not mean she planned to close any banks as alleged by some Belgrade media.
- Final discussion on ownership transformation law planned for Wednesday has been postponed until further notice.
- Main condition for speedy exports to European Union markets is extending credits to export-oriented production, Serbian government central coordination team said.
- European bank for financing railway rolling stock Eurofima will grant a credit to Yugoslav railways to improve its efficiency.
- Two Zajedno coalition leaders Zoran Djindjic and Vesna Pesic have not yet extended their explicit support to the candidacy of third leader Vuk Draskovic as Zajedno presidential candidate.
- World congress on rehabilitation on psychiatry will be held in Belgrade from August 27 to 30.
NASA BORBA
- The U.S does not support elections for Kosovo Albanian parallel parliament, says U.S. charge d'affaires Richard Miles.
- Kosovo is an internal affair of Serbia and Yugoslavia, says Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic in talks with U.N. Under Secretary Bernard Millet.

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and Montengrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic reached an agreement for deputies of Montenegro's ruling Democratic Party of Socialists to support the Serbian president's passage to federal office, paper learns.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Serbian republican elections will be held in November, according to the paper's sources within the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia.
- Kosovo Albanian shot dead Monday evening by unidentified terrorists in the village of Loznice in Kosovo.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic and Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic received U.N. Human Rights Rapporteur Elisabeth Rehn.
- Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic held talks with businessmen of Niksic municipality on Tuesday.
- London Berliner bank unblocked its 17-million dollar loan to Montenegrin shipping company Jugooceanija for the purchase of new vessels.

- Saltworks Solana Bajo Sekulic from Ulcinj is ready for a record production of 30,000 tonnes of salt. However, the companys' economic situation is bad due to uncontrolled imports of salt from Romania, Ukraine and Bosnia. -- Belgrade newsroom + 381 11 222 4305
